title: HD 303514 eclipses show common timing changes in eight TESS sectors from 2019 to 2026
abstract: We measure 15 complete eclipses of HD 303514 in eight TESS sectors from 2019 to 2026. The times change by about 100 minutes relative to the reference ephemeris. Separate constant periods for the two eclipse types give chi-square 387.76 for 11 degrees of freedom. Common timing waves near 222.7 and 600.2 days fit almost equally well, with chi-square 13.80 and 14.37 for 8 degrees of freedom. The tested opposite-sign wave fits much worse. Two 2021 events from sector 36 add data not used in the prior eclipse-loss study. Shape, baseline, pixel, omitted-sector and correlated-noise tests retain the timing changes. The data support a third body but do not select its orbit. Circular light-travel-time fits require extreme mass functions. Numerical eccentric light-time searches with an inner mass of 5 solar masses also fit poorly at ordinary stellar masses under nominal errors; this physical test weakens with larger shared errors. A future model must include possible dynamical timing delays. We give checked input hashes, original code, derived times, noise tests, figures and nominal forecasts. Limits include sparse coverage, selected error models, reduction shifts up to 16 minutes, no second instrument, and no joint three-body fit.

display.caption: Both eclipse types change time. Timing waves near 223 and 600 days fit almost equally well. The shaded region shows nominal future curves, not confidence bands. The period profile uses the stated empirical models and error estimates.

Alternative reductions retain the timing changes. A sector error in the covariance reduces but does not remove the constant-period discrepancy. The circular dynamical calculation is a leading-order diagnostic, not an outer-orbit fit.
The 15 accepted local eclipse windows and empirical profile fits. Flux samples come from external QLP data. Each event has its own depth, width and baseline.
